uart.signal: the committed tests/fixtures/nrf54lm20a-snake.elf boots in-sim and UARTE20 EasyDMA reaches the capture sink; the asserted lines carry the chip's OWN geometry and map (rram=2036K ram=511K, p3@0x500D8600), all of which are wrong on the nRF54L15 profile this one would most plausibly be copied from
uart.lane: core-ci: cargo test -p labwired-core --test strict_onboarding (the gate EXECUTES examples/nrf54lm20a-snake/io-smoke.yaml through the CLI and fails the board if any assertion fails)

spi.signal: SPIM22 EasyDMA drives an RM67162 AMOLED and the run is judged on the PICTURE, not the transaction: a display_region assertion requires ink in the 240x520 play area and requires the never-addressed 16-row strip below it to be EXACTLY black. Verified to discriminate -- setting DCXCNT to 0 in the firmware, so no byte is ever framed as a command, leaves every UART assertion passing and takes the play area to 0.0% inked.
spi.lane: core-ci: cargo test -p labwired-core --test strict_onboarding (the gate EXECUTES examples/nrf54lm20a-snake/io-smoke.yaml through the CLI and fails the board if any assertion fails)
spi.note: the D/C line is driven by the CONTROLLER (PSEL.DCX + DCXCNT), not a GPIO, so this also proves the nRF54L SPIM's hardware data/command path end to end.

i2c.gap: TWIM21 is declared at 0x500C7000 and uses the same nrf54l_twim model the nRF54L15 smart-ring lane proves, but no nrf54lm20a manifest or firmware wires an I2C device.
